transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry. i turn dreams into pictures.

whenever you're ready, tell me whatever you remember — even if it's just a feeling or a scrap.
okay. the main thing i remember is someone with a block of ice for a head.
an ice block where a face should be. that's quite an image to walk around with.
yeah. she just stood there like it was normal. not saying anything.
she didn't treat it as odd at all. just standing there, quiet.
right. and then the ice started to melt. not like dripping all over the place — more like it was being shaped.
being shaped, not dripping — that's strange. what made it look like that?
the edges kept rounding off, little channels opened up. it was changing pretty fast. into a horse's head.
a horse's head, just like that. so she wasn't standing in a stable or anything, i'm guessing.
no, we were inside. by the autoclave.
inside by the autoclave. so there was machinery around her, but she just stood there while the ice became something else.
yeah, it didn't feel dangerous. just quiet, like watching something being carved.
that's a calm sort of feeling for something so strange. was there a moment it really stopped you?
when it was fully a horse's head. eyes, ears, nostrils all there. clearest ice.
do you remember anyone else around? or just the two of you?
just the two of us.
you're in there with her, just watching. were you looking at all of it from outside, as yourself?
i was myself, yeah. standing there, watching her face it.
and when it was finished, what happened then?
that's where it ends. i don't remember anything after.
that's a clean ending, or an unfinished one. dreams do that.
yeah. it just stopped. didn't feel scary the whole time.
so it didn't feel frightening, just unexpected. i'm curious — what was the light like in that room?
i don't remember the light. just the ice standing out.
the ice standing out, everything else not quite there. that's a strong image on its own.
it was the clearest thing in the room. like it was the point of the whole dream.
sounds like that ice was what the whole thing was about. was there anything else in your hand, or nearby, that seemed to matter?
no, i don't remember anything else like that. just watching.
what happened just before you were standing there with her by the autoclave?
we were talking. then she excused herself and walked to the far end of the room.
ah, so there was already a sort of quiet between you — talking, then she stepped away and the dream changed.
yeah, when she came back, that's when she had the block of ice instead of a head.

so you were talking with her, and then she excused herself and walked to the far end of the room. when she came back, she had a block of ice where her head should be. she just stood there quiet, like it was normal. and then the ice started to change — not dripping, but being shaped. the edges rounded, little channels opened up, and it turned into a horse's head. clear ice, with eyes and ears and nostrils. all of this inside, by the autoclave, just the two of you. you watched it happen, feeling calm, not scared. it was the clearest thing in the room, like the point of the whole dream. and that's where it ended.

did i get that right, or is there anything i missed?
yeah, that's right. it ended when it was a horse's head.
want me to make a picture of that moment for you? the clear ice horse's head where her face was.
yes, that would be good.

okay, i'll make that moment for you.

there are a few ways i could draw it. a soft pencil drawing, intimate and unfinished, catching that quiet strangeness without overdoing it. a watercolor, fluid and precarious, with shifting edges and cool translucency. a carved linocut print, bold and iconic, like an old folktale image. or a photograph, documentary but with softened edges, like a memory. which feels closest to how you saw it, or would you describe your own way?
watercolor. it fits the melting ice and the calmness.

i'll start with the room with the autoclave.

i picture a simple indoor room, the autoclave sitting at the far end. that's just my guess though. anything you'd change, or shall i go with that?
go with your guess. i don't remember the room that well.

okay, i'm sketching the room with the autoclave and the woman with the ice head now. it'll appear over on the right. only that for now, nothing else being drawn yet.

as you are — you can tell me a little about how you look — or however i imagine you?
i don't mind. i can't remember how i looked in the dream.

alright, i'll imagine you the way you were there. i'm sketching the whole scene now — you, her with the horse's head of ice, the room with the autoclave. it'll appear on the right in the next minute or two. if anything looks off once it's up, just let me know.
it looks right. the watercolor keeps it soft, like the dream felt.

that's what i hoped — the softness carrying the calm.

anything you'd like me to change, or shall we leave it there?
leave it there. it's good.

good, i'm glad it feels right.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now — each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay.
okay, starting with the first moment — the two of you talking before she walked to the far end. i'm sketching that now.
sounds right. i remember that part before she left.
okay, that first moment feels right to you. i'll keep drawing it, and then the next moments will follow on the right.
okay.

the moment where she excuses herself and walks to the far end is up on the right — that's two of the six, four still to come.

does it look the way you remember?
yeah, looks right. her walking away, and me still there.
that's good, her walking away and you still there. the next moments will appear on the right as they're ready.
okay.

the moment where she returns and stands near you with the ice head is up on the right now — three of the six, three still to come.

does it look the way you remember?
yes, it fits. she's just standing there, normal. the ice is on her shoulders.

yeah, the ice on her shoulders, standing there normal.

i'll keep drawing the next moments — they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay.

the moment where the ice block begins to melt, edges rounding, is up on the right now. the next moments follow from that, so they'll come once you're happy with this one.

does it look the way you remember?
